messages:
anita: Quick sync: multiple customers reporting fragmentation in quota dashboards again. Different SDKs are producing different attribution shapes and the charts are showing split lines.
peter: Can you paste an example?
anita: From logs: `x-rw-attr: acct=team-alpha` vs `X-Redwood-Meta: {"acct":"team-alpha","route":"beta"}` and `acct_key=team-alpha`.
zhou: Same story as previous threads but we're seeing it across more regions now. I think the routing policy rollout amplified it because fallback paths surface the alt headers.
samir: Two orthogonal fixes: 1) SDK convergence to a single canonical header, 2) ingestion-side coalescing that maps equivalent headers into a canonical attribution id for Console/telemetry while preserving raw for billing.
anita: Ingestion coalescing seems attractive because it buys time and avoids touching hot SDK paths. But we need to be careful about auditability and reproducibility.
peter: Agreed. Proposal: add a lightweight deterministic "attr-signature" header produced by the SDK that is a short stable string (HMAC of acct+route with service salt). Ingestion can use that to coalesce buckets without parsing arbitrary shapes. SDKs emit canonical textual header as well, but ingestion trusts signature for merge.
zhou: Nice: signatures are small, constant-size, and avoid parsing JSON in the hot path. But rolling that out requires SDK changes in TS/Py/Go.
samir: SDK plan: TS & Py add middleware to emit `X-Redwood-Attr-Sig: v1:abc123` when they can compute acct+route. When unknown, they omit. Go will add a zero-cost path: if token contains acct claim, compute sig without mallocs. All behind opt-in env flags for canary.
anita: Console/ingestion plan: add a coalescing layer that uses attr-sig -> canonical attribution map. If attr-sig absent, fall back to heuristics (acct match, route missing rule). Keep raw buckets for billing pipeline unchanged; coalesced view only affects Console visualizations and telemetry aggregates.
peter: UX: Console should show a small pill "coalesced view" when applied and a table that expands to show underlying raw keys. Also add a timeline heatmap showing adoption of attr-sig per client (TS/Py/Go) so customers can track migration.
zhou: Telemetry: emit a metric `ingest.attr_sig.adoption` by sdk_language and region. Also emit `ingest.coalesce.ratio` (coalesced_visits/total_visits) so we can monitor drift.
samir: Tests & rollout: synthetic runner that sends mixed header shapes with and without attr-sig. Run canary for 6h 10% traffic, verify coalesced viz equals sum(raw) and that billing remains unchanged.
anita: Security: attr-sig must be HMAC with per-region key stored in KMS. Validate in ingestion with KMS or locally cached verification keys. If signature validation fails, ingestion should ignore signature and mark an anomaly metric.
peter: Backcompat: SDKs should continue to send legacy headers for 2 weeks after sig rollout. Migration docs + CLI check tool (`rw-check-attr`) for customers to validate headers. Example curl we can add to support playbook:

```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." -H "X-Redwood-Attr-Sig: v1:abc123" -H "X-Redwood-Meta: acct=team-alpha;route=beta" https://api.redwood.ai/generate
```

zhou: I'll prototype the ingestion coalescer this week. Samir, can you draft the SDK middleware for TS? Anita, can you take Py? Peter, you take Go shim.
samir: Yep, TS PR will be middleware + unit tests + an E2E synthetic. Will default to OFF via REDWOOD_EMIT_ATTR_SIG=0 for canary.
anita: Py PR similarly behind env flag, with a helper in `redwood.util.attr` to compute sig.
peter: Go shim will try to compute from token claim cheaply; if not present, skip. Benchmarking will be added.
err-bot: NOTE: scheduled canary job created: ingest-coalesce-canary pipeline #9921 -> start 2026-06-01T01:00Z (6h, 10% traffic).
zhou: Console UX: add "adoption heatmap" tile and a drilldown per SDK. Also a tooltip explaining coalesced view and link to migration docs.
anita: Support playbook: how to inspect headers, how to read adoption tile, steps to opt-in SDKs, and rollback instructions. I'll draft and circulate.
samir: PRs will reference this thread. We'll reconvene after canary results.
anita: Action items: Samir (TS PR + tests), Anita (Py PR + util), Peter (Go shim + bench), Zhou (ingest coalescer + console tile), ops (run canary pipeline). Recheck in 48h.
peter: Opening Go PR now: https://github.com/redwood/sdk-go/pull/149 (draft).
samir: Draft TS PR: https://github.com/redwood/sdk-ts/pull/537 (wip).
anita: Draft Py PR soon. Thanks everyone.
